subject: Home range meta-analysis and hard borders

messages.author: f2a74e4c4c138715
messages.subject: Home range meta-analysis and hard borders
parts:
Hello, apologies - I feel like all my questions are so basic but I really want to follow the process right. 

Two unrelated questions:
1. Home range meta analysis - so I've produce AKDE home ranges for all of my animals. I subset each one from the master dataset and went through the home range estimation process for each one individually. I wasn't sure if I could have ran this from the master dataset but figured some might need different mitigation measures based on their data so I did each one independently. Now I'm working through the home range meta analysis process so I can compare between groups (e.g. age, region, habitat, etc) but noticed I need to use a consolidated dataset so that AKDE's are calculated on the same grid for all individuals. How then does this affect the nuance of the AKDE's calculated independently whereby different mitigation measures have been applied for certain individuals (e.g. bootstrapping for small sample sizes)? Wont combining them all and calculating AKDE's using a standard method produce different results?

2. Some of my AKDE's extend into the pacific ocean even though the species Im tracking is completely terrestrial albeit occupies near-coastal environments. Therefore I want to make the land mass a hard border in calculating AKDE's. So really just want to check that the way to do that is in the AKDE function using a shapefile of the landmass (i.e a SpatialPolygonsDataFrame) in the SP argument along with the SP.in = TRUE as I want the locations and home range to be inside its boundaries. 

Thank you so much for the support in using this package and process. 

Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Home range meta-analysis and hard borders
parts:
Hi Chris,

Sorry for the delay.
  1. For meta() you don't need them to be on the same grid. But for pkde(), overlap(), encounter(), cde() you do. Calculating them on the same grid doesn't hurt anything, as long as the grid is sufficient to capture the details of the distribution, which the default grid will do.
  2. Yes.
Best,
Chris
